newsitem.title: INDIA: Start of India's global pepper exchange delayed.
newsitem.headline: Start of India's global pepper exchange delayed.

text.p: India's ambitious plans to start the country's first international pepper futures exchange by the end of April have been delayed due to procedural snags, trade officials said on Thursday.

"We have not been able to fix a date due to procedural problems," a spokesman of the Indian Pepper and Spices Trade Association (IPSTA) told Reuters by phone from Kochi in the southern Indian state of Kerala.
In February, the Food Ministry announced that the country's first international peppers futures exchange and clearing house would start functioning at Kochi by April.

India's cabinet decided in the second half of 1995 to upgrade the domestic futures commodity exchange, run by IPSTA in Kochi, into an international exchange. The domestic exchange has 140 members and the annual volume of trade is about six billion rupees.
The spokesman said IPSTA had sought the Reserve Bank of India's permission for banks and financial institutions to become clearing members.
"RBI says it has no objection to banks and financial institutions becoming clearing members, the spokesman said.
"But at the same time they say they (banks) should not have any risk exposure and rules and regulations of the clearing house should not hold on them any risk on account of default," he said.
He said RBI had suggested that applications from banks to become members of the clearing house would be considered on merit.
IPSTA officials said there was not much risk for the financial institutions by participating in the clearing house as they would be lending service to their clients.
"At most, the risk will be limited to the equity which they have invested in the clearing house. That being the case such a clause does not give the right signal," said one senior IPSTA official.
He said it was not clear what criterion RBI would apply to each individual application.
"This one-to-one approach may not be very satisfactory because it is time-consuming," he said.
The spokesman said a clearing house was compulsory for the futures exchange.
"So we cannot launch it unless institutional clearing members or at least a clearing bank is in place," he said.
The spokesman said IPSTA was seeking a clarification from RBI and was at present not in a position to set a tentative date for the start of the exchange.
He said the federal government was also keen that the exchange should start in April so that based on its success futures trading could be thrown open to other commodities.
"All efforts are being made by IPSTA to get the international exchange started as early as possible," he said.
India annually produces about one third of the world's total pepper output of 180,000 tonnes. The other major producers include Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam.
